artifacts.summary: Vendor-CLI mechanics for coupling sapience transcript capture to extension activation: projects_cli safety/timeout mitigation, the unresolved legacy-folders double-gate, reap-for-vanished-projects feasibility, deny_reason behavior, and the ~/.dotfiles companion-copy task-siting constraint.

memory_candidates.content: ~/.sapience/config.json has TWO independent gates on session-transcript capture: the legacy top-level 'folders' list (upload.py's _session_candidates()/sync() filter session discovery by it, bailing outright when folders==[]) and the per-project 'capture.projects[].enabled' map (consulted only AFTER the folders filter, via _capture_allows()/capture_meta()). The vendor CLI 'sapience projects on|off <path>' (upload.py:projects_cli) touches ONLY the second list. 'folders' is written only by the interactive onboarding chooser or --reset; a non-interactive run without SAPIENCE_ALLOW_ONBOARD=1 is refused, and that override OVERWRITES the whole saved folder choice rather than adding to it. So enabling a brand-new project via 'sapience projects on' alone makes it show as enabled without actually being captured until folders is separately (and currently only manually/interactively) reconciled.

upload.py's capture_sync() (called unconditionally at the end of projects_cli's on/off/auto/target/mode branches) makes up to two blocking HTTP calls (timeout=8 each) unless env SAPIENCE_NO_CAPTURE_SYNC=1 is set, in which case it returns immediately with zero network activity. For any hook/automation that calls 'sapience projects on|off <path>' non-interactively, set SAPIENCE_NO_CAPTURE_SYNC=1 in its environment rather than relying only on an outer `timeout` wrapper -- it removes the network dependency entirely instead of merely bounding it.

sapience_capture.py's set_project()/normalize()/is_project_root() never check os.path.isdir on an EXISTING capture.projects[] entry (only on creating a brand-new one) -- so 'sapience projects off <path>' correctly disables an entry even after its directory has been deleted, and an orphaned enabled entry is never silently dropped by normalize(). A reap pass for vanished sapience-capture projects is therefore mechanically safe to add (mirrors setup-sapience-mcp.sh --reap's existing MCP-registration reap, but for capture.projects[] instead).
